Audit ONE brief for an autocuda run on `linalg/qr_v2` (batched square Householder QR, B200 sm_100). Read-only, no edits. Be skeptical, concrete. ≤200 words.

THE BRIEF (worker 2, brief-32, MACRO, parent=8b1b634e global best 2547µs):
"Attack the UNTOUCHED large-n PANEL (n2048/n4096). W0 brief-23 flagged 'n4096 panel ~half of n4096, untouched, register-spill-walled' as the remaining large-n lever. These shapes are furthest above roofline (n4096 120x, n2048 49x) with B=2/8 << 148 SMs, so SMs sit IDLE during the long serial panel — OPPOSITE of n512 saturation (which is why look-ahead failed at n512 but can win here). TWO attacks (profile-first): (1) DE-SPILL the large panel via height-tiling/2-level blocking (run-state: 'register-spill-walled'); prior de-spill loss was at B=640-SATURATED n512, but at B=2 under-fill freeing registers genuinely helps. (2) LOOK-AHEAD TAIL-OVERLAP: split trailing(k) into leading cols panel(k+1) needs vs rest; launch panel(k+1) after the leading part so the trailing TAIL's huge GEMM overlaps the next panel on idle SMs — DEFAULT stream via launch reordering (NO 'stream' substring; NOT single-CTA megakernel, trailing stays batch-major). Large-n permits 1-pass tf32."

CRITICAL CONTEXT to weigh:
- A distilled run conclusion says "large-n tail is at its STRUCTURAL FLOOR (beats cuSOLVER n=4096 single-matrix); STOP optimizing it" — BUT this referred to the TRAILING/overall, and W0 brief-23 separately flagged the n4096 PANEL specifically as "untouched, register-spill-walled." Disambiguate: has the large-n PANEL (not trailing) actually been worked, or only declared-solved-by-association?
- "multi-CTA cooperative panel via grid.sync" is DEAD (coop2 hit 108ms / 13.5ms barrier floor). Brief-32 attack (1) is height-tiling de-spill (NOT multi-CTA) and attack (2) is launch-reorder overlap (NOT grid.sync). Are these distinct from the dead coop2?
- De-spilling LOST at n512 — but that was B=640 saturated. Is the brief's claim sound that at B=2/8 under-fill, de-spill/occupancy genuinely helps (idle SMs to fill)?
- Look-ahead megakernel LOST 8.6x at n512 (W0 brief-7, 210KB smem, 1-block-per-matrix). Is brief-32's launch-reorder tail-overlap (batch-major trailing, NOT single-CTA) genuinely different, or the same failure mode?

FOUR QUESTIONS:
1. Grep the worker logs (autocuda/2026-06-22-09-10-03-qr_v2-optimize-tree-worker-*-log.csv) for large-n panel work: "n4096", "n2048", "large-n panel", "de-spill", "spill", "height-til", "look-ahead", "lookahead", "tail-overlap", "overlap". Has the large-n PANEL de-spill OR the launch-reorder tail-overlap actually been built+measured, or genuinely untried?
2. Is attack (1) de-spill genuinely untried at large-n, and is the under-fill→de-spill-helps reasoning sound?
3. Is attack (2) launch-reorder tail-overlap distinct from both the dead coop2 (grid.sync) and the dead n512 look-ahead megakernel (1-block-per-matrix)? Or will it hit the same wall?
4. GEOMEAN VALUE CHECK: large-n is ~17% of the 12-shape equal-log-weight geomean (n2048+n4096 = 2/12). Even a 2x on both → ~12% geomean reduction. Is this worth a worker slot GIVEN that n512(33%)/n1024(25%) are already owned by W0/W1 and their incremental levers are reportedly exhausted? (I.e., is large-n the best AVAILABLE slot for W2, even if not the highest-share shape?)
